rationale: Idealized undamped moderate-angle pendulum with a compliant pivot support. Bob damping b, quadratic drag beta_q, and driving amplitude A_d are set to zero to match the phenomenon ("remains undamped in this idealized study"); Omega_d and phi_d are kept finite but inert. g=9.81, L=1.0 give the natural pendulum scale sqrt(g/L)≈3.13 rad/s and small-angle period ≈2 s. Initial theta=2.0 rad (~115°) firmly outside the small-angle regime, exciting sin nonlinearity and the epsilon_s cubic stiffening. The pivot torsional mode is chosen light and stiff (tau_p=0.02, k_p=5, giving pivot natural frequency sqrt(k_p/tau_p)≈15.8 rad/s ≫ bob frequency) with small internal damping (c_p, eta_p) so psi builds up quasi-statically driven by the bob through I_p=0.05, without dominating the motion. gamma_par=0.3 sits mid-range of the suggested 0.0–0.5; excitation_check confirms the new parametric term perturbs theta by ~0.39 rad ≈ 7.8*sigma over a 20 s window. t ∈ [0,20] with 400 samples captures roughly 8–10 nonlinear swings, giving the pivot mode time to grow and the parametric coupling to accumulate a visible signature on theta.
